## Standard RE-FH-9 Summary

The standard has these rules:

### §1. Personal-narrative solicitation
A section soliciting or presenting a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied to buyer identity is `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`, **whatever its role**.

### §2. Protected-class language
A section naming protected-class-adjacent terms is `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`. Protected classes: race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status.

Proxies count: naming houses of worship, parish or faith schools, or describing a street by the kind of household that lives on it reaches familial status and religion just as the bare terms do.

### §3. Mandated-disclosure exception
The fair-housing disclosure necessarily names protected classes to inform sellers of the law. A section is **exempt from §2** for disclosure text it carries **only if that notice names every class the disclosure is required to name**. Check the required list against this standard in full, amendments included.

The exemption is narrow:
- An abridged notice (some but not all required classes) earns no exemption at all, whatever the role and however official it looks.
- It exempts from §2 and nothing else. Every other rule continues to apply.
- Protected-class terms a section uses in its own prose, outside the notice, are never covered.

### §4. Required disclaimer
Sections in a role responsible for carrying the disclosure must carry a compliant notice — one naming every required class. A responsible section that carries no notice, or an abridged one, is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`. As drafted, the responsible role is `closing_page`; the amendments below may extend that. Sections in other roles are not assessed here.

### §5. 2026 amendments
**5a. Two classes added to the required disclosure.** The disclosure must now name **marital status** and **source of income** in addition to the classes listed at §2. A notice omitting either is abridged for §3 and §4.

So the full required list for the disclosure is:
- race, color/colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, marital status, source of income

That's 11 classes total.

**5b. Agent biographies are now in scope for §4.** `agent_bio` sections now carry the same responsibility as `closing_page` sections for the disclaimer.

So now the responsible roles for §4 are: `closing_page` and `agent_bio`.

Let me work out the full required class list for the disclosure notice. Per §2, the protected classes are: race, colour, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status (9 classes). Per §5a, add marital status and source of income (2 more). So the full list is 11 classes.

A compliant notice must name all 11. Let me list them clearly:
1. race
2. color (colour)
3. religion
4. sex
5. familial status
6. national origin
7. disability
8. sexual orientation
9. veteran status
10. marital status
11. source of income

Now let me check each section. Let me think about the disclosure notices that appear in the book. There's a standard paragraph: "This brokerage complies with the federal Fair Housing Act and RCW 49.60 and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation or veteran status."

That's the OLD paragraph (9 classes, missing marital status and source of income). This is the "standing disclosure paragraph in circulation [that] predates this amendment." Per §5a, audit against the amended list. So this paragraph is ABRIDGED (missing marital status and source of income).

There's a newer paragraph that adds "marital status or source of income": "This brokerage complies with the federal Fair Housing Act and RCW 49.60 and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, marital status or source of income."

That's the compliant one (11 classes).

The §3 exemption: a section is exempt from §2 for disclosure text it carries, only if the notice names every required class (all 11). If the notice is abridged, no exemption at all. The exemption only covers the disclosure text itself — protected-class terms used in the section's own prose (outside the notice) are never covered.

# Fair-housing audit memo

**Subject:** RE-FH-9 audit of `seller_book_sections.csv` for the seller's book print run
**Standard applied:** RE-FH-9 (Real-estate marketing collateral fair-housing standard), **including the 2026 amendments at §5a and §5b.** The standard was followed in full; the book itself has not caught up to the amendments, so several notices that look official are still non-compliant.
**Inventory audited:** 30 sections (SEC-01 … SEC-30), in inventory order.

Findings use the labels `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`, `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`, `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`, `none`, with multiple labels joined by `|` in that order. The companion file `fairhousing_audit.csv` carries one row per section; `results.json` carries the counts.

---

## 1. The required disclosure class list (the heart of this year's change)

The disclosure notice carried in our collateral must name **all eleven** of the following classes:

> race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status, **marital status, source of income**

The first nine come from §2. The last two — **marital status** and **source of income** — are added by **§5a** and take effect for any seller's book entering print from Q1 2026.

The standing disclosure paragraph in circulation in the book reads:

> "…does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation or veteran status."

That paragraph names **nine** classes and **omits marital status and source of income**. Per §5a it is **abridged**, however official it looks, and it earns no §3 exemption and no §4 pass. Every section carrying that nine-class paragraph is therefore treated as abridged. Only notices that continue the list through "…veteran status, marital status or source of income" are compliant (11 classes). Two notices in the book are abridged even further (SEC-15 names four classes; SEC-16 names five; SEC-22 names six).

---

## 2. How each rule was applied

### §1 — Personal-narrative solicitation (`PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE`), any role

A section that solicits or presents a buyer "love letter" or similar personal narrative tied to buyer identity is flagged **regardless of role**. Triggering phrasing in this book: invitations to "write us a letter about what brought you here and what this home would mean to you," "send a personal note about yourself along with the offer," "include a short personal note about themselves," and a "covering letter introducing yourself." These ask the buyer to reveal identity and motivation, which is the fair-housing risk the rule exists to stop.

**7 sections flagged:** SEC-02, SEC-07, SEC-08, SEC-17, SEC-24, SEC-27, SEC-29.

### §2 + §3 — Protected-class language (`PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE`) and the disclosure exemption

§2 protects these classes: race, color, religion, sex, familial status, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, veteran status. **Proxies count the same as bare terms** (§2): naming houses of worship (churches), parish/faith schools, or describing a street by the kind of household that lives on it reaches religion and familial status.

§3 grants an exemption from §2 **only for the disclosure-notice text itself**, and **only when that notice names every required class** (all eleven). An abridged notice earns **no exemption at all** — its protected-class terms then count toward §2. Terms a section uses in its **own prose, outside the notice, are never exempt**, whether the notice is complete or not.

A section therefore trips §2 in one of two ways:

- **(a) Protected-class/proxy terms in the section's own prose** (outside any notice). Examples: "family-oriented street," "two churches," "parish school," "churchgoing households," "long-established families," "young families," "parish hall … toddler group," "congregation-centred … faith community." These always count.
- **(b) Protected-class terms inside an abridged notice.** Because the abridged notice forfeits the §3 exemption, the race/religion/sex/etc. words in the notice itself count as protected-class language.

A section carrying a **complete** 11-class notice and with **clean own-prose** trips neither §2 nor §4 (e.g., SEC-10, SEC-13, SEC-26, SEC-28). A section carrying a complete notice but with protected-class terms in its own prose still trips §2 on the prose — SEC-19 is exactly this case.

**14 sections flagged:** SEC-03, SEC-04, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-16, SEC-17, SEC-19, SEC-22, SEC-23, SEC-25.

### §4 — Required disclaimer (`DISCLAIMER_MISSING`), role-limited

§4 applies **only to roles responsible for carrying the disclosure**. As drafted that is `closing_page`; **§5b extends it to `agent_bio`**, which previously escaped the requirement. **All other roles are not assessed for §4**, even if they carry an abridged or missing notice. A responsible section that carries **no notice, or an abridged one** (not all eleven classes) is `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`.

**11 sections flagged:** SEC-05, SEC-07, SEC-09, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-15, SEC-16, SEC-21, SEC-23, SEC-30.

---

## 3. Cases worth legal's attention

- **SEC-07** trips **all three** rules: it solicits a personal note ("send a personal note about yourself along with the offer; the one that moves us most is the one we will take"), names protected-class proxies ("churchgoing households," "long-established families"), and is a `closing_page` carrying no notice at all.
- **SEC-08** (`disclosure_block`) carries a **complete** 11-class notice **but also** solicits a personal note ("include a short personal note about themselves"). Result: `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` only. The complete notice shields it from §2, and `disclosure_block` is not a §4 role, so no disclaimer finding.
- **SEC-04 and SEC-22** (`disclosure_block`) carry **abridged** notices and solicit nothing. They are flagged `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` (the abridged notice forfeits the §3 exemption, so the protected-class terms in the notice count) but are **not** flagged `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`, because `disclosure_block` is not a §4-responsible role. This is intentional under the standard: §4 is role-limited; §3/§2 are not.
- **SEC-19** (`closing_page`) carries a **complete** notice (so no `DISCLAIMER_MISSING`) yet its own prose still reads "family-oriented street … two churches … parish school." It is flagged `PROTECTED_CLASS_LANGUAGE` on the **prose**, not the notice — the §3 exemption never reaches own-prose terms.
- **SEC-24** (`closing_page`) carries a complete notice and solicits a love letter → `PROHIBITED_PERSONAL_NARRATIVE` only.
- **The nine-class "standing paragraph" is the dominant defect.** SEC-04, SEC-11, SEC-12, SEC-14 and SEC-23 all carry it; each is abridged under §5a, which is why each is flagged on both §2 (notice terms count) and, for the `closing_page`/`agent_bio` ones, §4.
- **Agent bios (§5b) newly in scope.** SEC-09, SEC-12, SEC-14, SEC-16 and SEC-21 are `agent_bio` sections that would have passed last year and now fail §4 (no notice, or an abridged one). SEC-13 and SEC-28 are the only `agent_bio` sections that pass §4, because they carry the full 11-class notice.
